questions.stem: State the general formula of open-chain alkanes and list the first six members by name.
questions.modelAnswer: CnH2n+2; methane, ethane, propane, butane, pentane, hexane.

questions.stem: Explain, in two sentences, why cycloalkanes carry two fewer hydrogens than their open-chain equivalents.
questions.modelAnswer: Closing a carbon ring uses two bonding positions that open-chain members spend on hydrogen; cyclohexane therefore holds C6H12 where hexane holds C6H14.

questions.stem: Explain why alkane molecules show essentially no polarity.
questions.modelAnswer: Carbon and hydrogen have nearly matching electronegativities, so every C-H bond shares its pair almost evenly and the dipoles cancel across the symmetric molecule.

questions.stem: A hydrocarbon has formula C5H12. Classify it as alkane, cycloalkane or alkene and justify using the formulas.
questions.modelAnswer: C5H12 fits CnH2n+2, so it is an open-chain alkane - pentane; a cycloalkane of five carbons would be C5H10 and an alkene likewise C5H10.

questions.stem: Write the balanced equation for the complete combustion of methane.

questions.modelAnswer: Plentiful oxygen as the condition; carbon dioxide and water as the only products.

questions.stem: Explain why a limited oxygen supply changes the products of alkane combustion.
questions.modelAnswer: With too little oxygen the carbon cannot all reach the +4 oxidation state of carbon dioxide, so carbon monoxide or even soot forms instead, and less heat is released.

questions.stem: Write the balanced equation for the complete combustion of butane, C4H10.
questions.modelAnswer: 2C4H10 + 13O2 -> 8CO2 + 10H2O: carbons 8=8, hydrogens 20=20, and the 26 oxygen atoms supplied by 13 O2 divide as 16 into the eight CO2 and 10 into the ten H2O.

questions.stem: Explain why incomplete combustion releases less energy than complete combustion.
questions.modelAnswer: Carbon monoxide still stores usable oxidation energy that complete combustion would have released, so the limited-oxygen route pays out a smaller energy dividend.

questions.stem: A faulty boiler burns methane with a restricted air supply. Name the hazard gas and write its balanced formation equation within the combustion.
questions.modelAnswer: The hazard is carbon monoxide; within the combustion ledger, methane burning incompletely forms it as 2CH4 + 3O2 -> 2CO + 4H2O.
